what: Daily facts on where idle US-dollar cash can sit: bitcoin-backed preferred stocks beside a 4-week US Treasury bill, a government money market fund and USDC lending. Facts and arithmetic only. Not advice. Nothing here holds, moves or trades money.
numbers: Every number carries its source address and the date it is true for (as_of), or the formula and inputs it was worked out from. A number that could not be read is null, with the reason next to it. Nothing is filled in by hand.
stale: A number is stale when it is more than 4 days older than the build date. A worked-out number is stale when any of its inputs is.

formulas.yield_pct: stated_rate_pct * par_usd / close_usd: the yearly payout on the $100 par, as a percent of the last close. The issuer can change the stated rate.
formulas.worst_drop_pct: the largest fall, in percent, from a closing high to any later close, over the past year of daily closes
formulas.avg_volume_30d: mean shares traded per day over the newest 30 daily rows
formulas.schedule: the median gap between the last 6 pay dates: up to 4 days is every business day, 10-20 twice a month, 25-35 monthly, 80-100 quarterly
formulas.payments: pay dates on or before the build date, counted back to the last gap; a gap is a missing payment longer than the usual spacing (35 days, or 100 for quarterly payers, or 4 days once a security pays daily)
formulas.est_income_usd: round(amount_usd * yield_pct / 100 * days / 365, 2): simple interest at today's yield, before tax and fees, ignoring any change in price

inputs.amount_usd: the cash to place, in US dollars
inputs.days: how long it can stay placed
inputs.max_drop_pct: the biggest past-year price fall the owner will accept
inputs.kinds: what the account can hold: preferred, tbill, money_market, usdc_lending

compare.options: instruments whose kind is in kinds, whose yield is known, and whose worst drop is at or under max_drop_pct; sorted by yield, highest first, then by ticker
compare.excluded: every other instrument, with the plain reason it was left out
compare.benchmarks: always returned; holdable says whether the account can hold that kind

flags.price_moves: a listed preferred stock: its price moves every day and can fall below the $100 par, so the cash back can be less than the cash put in
flags.issuer_sets_rate: the issuer sets the dividend rate and can lower or skip it
flags.short_history: fewer than 90 trading days of prices, so the worst drop covers a short time
flags.thin_trading: the amount is more than 1% of an average day's trading (avg_volume_30d * close), or volume is unknown
flags.payment_gap: a payment was missed within the counted history
flags.no_payment_in_window: no known pay date falls within the chosen days
flags.stale: a number behind this row is more than 4 days old
flags.not_bank_insured: a money market fund: not a bank deposit and not insured by the FDIC
flags.smart_contract_risk: lending on a blockchain protocol: a software fault or hack can lose funds, and the rate changes block by block

sources.dividends, pay dates: Nasdaq dividend history, api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<ticker>/dividends; cross-checked against Strategy (STRC) and Strive (SATA)
sources.stated_rate_pct (SATA): Strive, strive.com/treasury dashboard. Strive dates the rate record to the day it was set, so it reads as stale until the next reset.
sources.stated_rate_pct (SATS): the SEC 8-K filing that set its terms; as_of is the day the filing was read
sources.tbill_4w: US Treasury daily bill rates (coupon-equivalent, 4 weeks), home.treasury.gov
sources.mmf_vmfxx: Nasdaq fund summary for VMFXX, 7-day yield. The response carries no date, so as_of is the day it was fetched.
sources.usdc_aave_v3: DefiLlama yields chart for the Aave v3 USDC pool on Ethereum, newest row
